items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S3143

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the education law, the public authorities law and the general
municipal law, in relation to authorizing tuition increases for the
State University of New York at Buffalo (Part A); to amend the education
law, in relation to the use of State University of New York at Buffalo
property (Part B); to amend the education law, the state finance law
and the tax law, in relation to the ability of the state university
trustees to purchase items and enter into contracts and agreements (Part
C); to amend the education law and the state finance law, in relation
to the distribution of money received from various sources related to
the State University of New York at Buffalo (Part D); and to amend the
education law, in relation to providing that certain lease of the State
University of New York at Buffalo need not be submitted to the attorney
general for his or her approval (Part E)

PURPOSE OF THE BILL:
To allow the University at Buffalo greater flexibility and autonomy in
regard to leasing, contracting, tuition increases, and the overall
daily operation at the University.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:
This act shall be known as the "UB 2020 Flexibility and Economic
Growth Act."

The legislation amends various sections of the Education Law, the
Public Authorities Law, the General Municipal Law, the State Finance
Law, and the Tax Law.

JUSTIFICATION:
Under the current economic climate, New York State must develop a
globally competitive, diversified economy. As New York's leading
public research university, the provisions detailed in this
legislation will transform the university at Buffalo into a model
twenty-first century public university. This transformation will
reinvigorate the Western New York region, spur the local economy and
improve the quality of life of its residents.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
S.2020-C of 2009/2010 Passed Senate

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
To be determined.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately, with provisions.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S3143A              REVISED 03/01/11

TITLE OF BILL:

An act
to amend the education law, the public authorities law and the general
municipal law, in relation to authorizing tuition increases for the
State University of New York at Buffalo (Part A); to amend the education
law, in relation to the use of State University of New York at Buffalo
property (Part B); to amend the education law, the state finance law
and the tax law, in relation to the ability of the state university
trustees to purchase items and enter into contracts and agreements (Part
C); to amend the education law and the state finance law, in relation
to the distribution of money received from various sources related to
the State University of New York at Buffalo (Part D); and to amend the
education law, in relation to providing that certain lease of the State
University of New York at Buffalo need not be submitted to the attorney
general for his or her approval (Part E)

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

PART A-TUITION, CAPITAL PROJECT AND CONSTRUCTION DELIVERY FLEXIBILITY

Section 1 modifies the New York State Education Law to allow the
University at Buffalo to establish starting with the 2011-2012
academic year differential tuition rates on a program by program,
class-year by class-year basis for undergraduate and graduate degree
granting programs, subject to an overall limitation based upon
indexed averages from other peer institutions and a semester
undergraduate limit of $375 and annual graduate limit of 15%. This
measure provides that the monies raised from any tuition increases
will be used exclusively for financial aid programs at the University
at Buffalo (this revenue would be used to provide financial aid to
ensure that no family making less than $60,000 a year would feel the
effect of the tuition increase) and for other University at Buffalo
related programs.

Sections 2 through 4 amend the Public Authorities Law to provide
maximum flexibility to the University at Buffalo for future capital
projects on its three campuses by allowing capital project financing
to proceed through campus-related nonprofit organizations, which
would be allowed to procure financing through the Dormitory Authority
of the State of New York.

Section 5 amends the General Municipal Law, the Finance Law and the
Education Law to exclude contracts for construction or renovation at
the University at Buffalo from certain multiple contractor and
bidding requirements, provided that wages paid to contractors
employed in conjunction with such construction or renovations shall
be at prevailing wage rates in accordance with the Labor Law, that
such construction or renovation complies with certain safety
precautions set forth in the Labor Law and
that a competitive selection process is employed in selecting
contractors to perform such construction or renovation.


Section 6 provides for certain construction or renovation projects at
the University at Buffalo to be undertaken pursuant to project labor
agreements, provided a study determines that a project labor
agreement will benefit such construction or renovation.

Section 7 provides for the creation and implementation of a diversity
plan for the University at Buffalo's UB 2020 initiative and for
periodic reporting regarding such diversity plan.

Sections 8 through 10 amend the General Municipal Law to allow future
capital projects on the three campuses of the University at Buffalo to
proceed through campus-related nonprofit organizations, through local
industrial development agencies.

Sections 11 and 12 amend the Education Law to increase the flexibility
afforded to the University at Buffalo for future capital projects by
allowing the University to utilize alternative, more cost
advantageous construction delivery models, including design/build,
and construction manager at risk, which are presently not allowed
under existing state law.

Section 13 requires the President of the University at Buffalo to
report annually to the Governor and the Legislature on the
effectiveness of these reforms.

PART B - LAND DISPOSITION FLEXIBILITY

Section 1 and 2 amend the Education Law to provide the University at
Buffalo with more flexibility to lease, acquire and dispose of land,
under the auspices of the SUNY Trustees, so as to maximize
educational and commercial development opportunities associated with
the UB's 2020 initiative.

Section 3 amends the Education Law to permit participation by the
University at Buffalo in public-private partnership arrangements with
public, nonprofit and business entities to further the objectives of
the University at Buffalo, including UB's 2020 initiative.

PART C - PROCUREMENT REFORM

Part C amends the Education Law, the State Finance Law and the Tax Law
to permit the University at Buffalo to purchase goods and services
without prior state agency approval.

Sections 1 through 4 and 8 are designed to provide greater autonomy to
the University at Buffalo in procuring goods and services, by
replacing State Comptroller procurement guidelines with guidelines
put forth by the SUNY Trustees and by exempting University at Buffalo
contracts from prior State Comptroller approval. Such transactions
would remain subject to post-audit review by the Comptroller.

Sections 5 and 6 are designed to allow SUNY-affiliated nonprofit
corporations to take advantage of centralized state purchasing.

Section 7 permits SUNY to establish rules for sole-source procurements
of goods and services, in lieu of state-mandated sole-source


procurement policies, in recognition of the unique nature of goods
and services procured by SUNY educational institutions.

PART D-RETENTION OF UNIVERSITY AT BUFFALO GENERATED FUNDS

Part D amends the Education Law and the State Finance Law to ensure
that revenue from University at Buffalo sponsored initiatives,
including all revenue generated through UB's 2020 initiative, remains
at the University at Buffalo to be used exclusively for University at
Buffalo programs.

PART E- ALUMNI ASSOCIATION LEASES

Part E amends the Education Law to conform the existing power of the
SUNY Trustees to lease University at Buffalo lands to its alumni
association with the procurement reforms set forth in Part C of the
proposed legislation.

JUSTIFICATION:

Under the current economic climate, New York State must develop a
globally competitive, diversified economy. As New York's leading
public research university, the provisions detailed in this
legislation will transform the University at Buffalo into a model
twenty-first century public university. This transformation will
reinvigorate the Western New York region, spur the local economy and
improve the quality of life of its residents.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately.
